questions.q: A field's documentation states 'AnnualRevenue is overwritten nightly by a Dun & Bradstreet integration; manual edits are lost within 24 hours.' Which category of metadata is this?
options: Technical metadata
Business metadata
Operational metadata
Reference data
questions.explain: This describes how the data behaves and moves in practice -- refresh timing and which job populates it -- which is operational metadata, distinct from the field's structural type (technical) or its business definition (business metadata).

questions.q: Why is Salesforce's Object Manager / Schema Builder, despite being accurate and always current, not a complete data dictionary on its own?
options: Because Object Manager often shows incorrect field types
Because it only covers technical metadata (field types, relationships) and doesn't capture business meaning or operational behavior
Because Schema Builder is only available in sandbox orgs
Because a full data dictionary cannot include any Salesforce-sourced information
questions.explain: Object Manager and Schema Builder generate accurate technical metadata directly from org configuration, but they say nothing about what a field means in business terms or how it behaves operationally -- both of which a real data dictionary also needs.

questions.q: What does Salesforce's Metadata API actually manage, as distinct from the REST or SOAP data APIs?
options: Record data such as Account and Opportunity field values
Org customizations and structural metadata, such as custom objects, fields, and layouts -- not record data itself
Only user login credentials and session tokens
Marketing campaign performance statistics
questions.explain: The Metadata API manages an org's customizations and metadata definitions (objects, fields, layouts, and more); actual record data is handled separately through the REST or SOAP data APIs.

questions.q: Why do business glossaries commonly become unreliable over time?
options: Because Salesforce automatically deletes glossary entries after 18 months
Because they are usually written once at project kickoff and never revisited as fields get repurposed, with no owner or review trigger tied to actual changes
Because business metadata cannot legally be documented outside the EU
Because glossaries are stored exclusively in Setup Audit Trail
questions.explain: Business metadata rarely comes from the platform automatically; without an assigned owner and a review process tied to real change events, a glossary written once quickly drifts out of sync with how fields are actually used.

questions.q: How does metadata management relate to the broader data-governance program?
options: They are the same thing, just different names for one program
Metadata management replaces the need for governance entirely once implemented
Governance decides what should be true about the data; metadata management records and keeps current the documentation describing what is actually true
Metadata management only applies to Salesforce orgs, while governance applies to every other system
questions.explain: Governance sets the rules (ownership, standardization, systems of record); metadata management is the practice of documenting and maintaining the technical, business, and operational facts that let those governance decisions be verified and acted on.
